description: Miami's only two-Michelin-star restaurant remains the city's most polished international fine-dining address. The counter-facing kitchen, signature Robuchon technique and Design District setting make it the clearest special-occasion booking for affluent gastronomes.
highlights: Two-Michelin-star French counter dining, open-kitchen theatre, polished service and a luxury Design District address.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; La Liste; Official website

description: Hiden is a tiny, password-access omakase counter hidden behind a Wynwood taco shop. Its flown-in Japanese seafood, hushed scale and La Liste recognition make it one of Miami's most exclusive culinary experiences.
highlights: Michelin-starred hidden omakase counter, imported Japanese seafood and one of Miami's toughest reservations.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; La Liste; Financial Times

description: COTE gives Miami a glamorous Korean steakhouse with Michelin-level polish. Dry-aged beef, tableside grilling, a serious beverage program and high-energy Design District design make it a natural choice for social luxury dining.
highlights: Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse with smokeless grills, dry-aged beef and a special-occasion crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; La Liste; Official website

description: Kevin Cory's five-seat Brickell Key counter predates Miami's omakase boom and remains one of the city's most singular meals. The evening unfolds slowly around pristine seafood, sake and soy from the chef's family brewery in Japan.
highlights: Ultra-intimate five-seat Japanese counter, La Liste recognition and a long-running cult reputation.
sources: La Liste; Time Out; Financial Times; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Thomas Keller's Surfside restaurant channels private-club glamour inside the restored Surf Club. It is polished, nostalgic and expensive in exactly the way Miami's most classic luxury diners expect.
highlights: Michelin-starred Thomas Keller restaurant with Art Deco glamour, tableside classics and Four Seasons polish.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club

description: Jeremy Ford's South of Fifth restaurant remains one of Miami Beach's defining tasting-menu experiences. The cooking is bold and modern, with a sleek room and an ambitious menu that draws on South Florida ingredients.
highlights: Michelin-starred contemporary tasting menu with a sleek South of Fifth room and sustainability recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; Official website

description: Michael Beltran's Coconut Grove flagship is one of Miami's most personal Michelin-starred restaurants. Cuban-American memory, French technique and tableside flourishes give the restaurant a sense of place without losing fine-dining precision.
highlights: Michelin-starred Coconut Grove dining with Cuban-American influences and polished tableside signatures.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Ogawa is a meticulous Little River omakase counter built around Japanese seafood, craft and hospitality. The small room, garden detail and high price point make it a major address in Miami's luxury sushi scene.
highlights: Michelin-starred 10-seat omakase counter, Japanese imports and one of Miami's most expensive sushi experiences.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Financial Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Chef Shingo Akikuni's Coral Gables counter is a refined Edomae-style omakase with a quietly luxurious tone. The small seating, seasonal seafood and strong service make it one of the best Japanese splurge dinners in the Miami market.
highlights: Michelin-starred Coral Gables omakase by a former Hiden chef, with a 14-seat counter and seasonal seafood.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Eater Miami; Financial Times; Official website

description: Le Jardinier brings Alain Verzeroli's vegetable-forward French cooking to the Miami Design District. Its elegant room, seasonal menu and proximity to L'Atelier make it a refined but slightly softer luxury option.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern French dining with vegetable-forward cooking beneath L'Atelier in the Design District.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; Official website

description: Juan Manuel Barrientos' Brickell restaurant translates Colombian cuisine into an immersive fine-dining journey. It is theatrical, polished and memorable, especially for diners looking for Latin American fine dining rather than another Miami steakhouse or sushi counter.
highlights: Michelin-starred Colombian tasting menu with immersive presentations and a Brickell riverside location.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Eater Miami; Official website

description: This intimate room inside the Carillon Miami Wellness Resort offers a compact, highly polished tasting-menu experience. French technique, global references and a resort setting make it one of Miami Beach's more discreet Michelin-starred dinners.
highlights: Michelin-starred tasting menu inside Carillon Miami Wellness Resort, with French technique and a small-room format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Official website

description: Boia De is a compact Buena Vista dining room with national acclaim and a loyal local following. Its inventive Italian-leaning cooking, superb wine list and unfussy setting make it feel more personal than many of Miami's glossier rooms.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern Italian-American cooking, creative pastas and a small high-demand dining room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Time Out; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Los Félix gives Coconut Grove a soulful, ingredient-driven Mexican restaurant centered on heirloom corn and traditional technique. It is relaxed for a starred restaurant, but the sourcing, beverages and culinary point of view make it essential.
highlights: Michelin-starred Mexican cooking with heirloom corn, nixtamalization and a natural-wine sensibility.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Mutra became one of the biggest stories of the 2026 Florida Michelin Guide when it earned a star in North Miami. Chef Raz Shabtai's contemporary kosher Middle Eastern cooking gives the city a distinctive luxury dining address outside the usual beach and Design District circuits.
highlights: New 2026 Michelin star, contemporary kosher Middle Eastern cooking and a North Miami setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Living; Resy; NBC Miami; Official website

description: Sunny's has quickly become Miami's most compelling new-school steakhouse. The banyan-shaded Little River setting, raw bar, martini culture and serious cooking make it feel both glamorous and locally rooted.
highlights: Michelin-selected steakhouse with raw bar, martini service, a banyan courtyard and major national acclaim.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out; Robb Report; Condé Nast Traveler; Official website

description: MILA Omakase narrows the larger MILA universe into an intimate Japanese counter with Filipino and Mediterranean inflections. It is expensive, theatrical and design-forward, matching Miami Beach's appetite for high-end Japanese dining with a strong sense of style.
highlights: Design-led omakase counter inside MILA, with Japanese technique, Filipino details and a luxury Miami Beach setting.
sources: Financial Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Francis Mallmann's restaurant at Faena Miami Beach remains a defining hotel-dining room for fire, theatre and South American glamour. It is not a quiet culinary temple, but it is exactly the kind of polished resort restaurant affluent visitors book for a big Miami night.
highlights: Faena Miami Beach dining room with live-fire Argentine cooking, dramatic design and luxury-hotel service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Time Out; Official website

description: Pao gives Faena a high-design Asian dining room with a strong sense of Miami spectacle. Paul Qui's menu, the Damien Hirst unicorn and the hotel's theatrical service culture make it a natural choice for affluent diners who want dinner to feel like an event.
highlights: Faena Miami Beach Asian destination with dramatic art, glamorous interiors and a polished luxury-hotel crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Time Out; Official website

description: Massimo Bottura's Miami outpost brings playful Italian cooking to The Moore in the Design District. The room is bright, stylish and social, while the menu is serious enough to function as a luxury alternative to the city's tasting-menu circuit.
highlights: Michelin-selected Design District Italian restaurant from Massimo Bottura with playful tasting options and pop-art design.
sources: Michelin Guide; Miami Design District; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Palma is a candlelit Little Havana restaurant built around contemporary tasting-menu ambition rather than Miami scene value. The narrow concrete room, personal cooking and date-night intensity give it a refined edge in a neighborhood better known for casual Cuban classics.
highlights: Michelin-selected contemporary tasting-menu restaurant with a candlelit Little Havana room and serious culinary ambition.
sources: Michelin Guide; Official website; En Primeur Club

description: Krüs Kitchen is a Coconut Grove favorite for seasonal cooking, natural wine and a sustainability-minded supply chain. It is less formal than the starred restaurants downstairs and nearby, but its sourcing and beverage culture keep it firmly in the affluent dinner conversation.
highlights: Michelin Green Star-awarded seasonal restaurant with natural wines, local sourcing and a relaxed Coconut Grove setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; OpenTable; Hungry Post; Official website

description: Milos brings the global Greek seafood formula to South of Fifth with pristine fish, polished service and a bright Mediterranean room. It is a reliable luxury choice for diners who want seafood, wine and a social Miami Beach atmosphere without a tasting-menu commitment.
highlights: High-end Greek seafood, whole fish, polished service and a prime South of Fifth location.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Time Out; Official website

description: Makoto has long been one of Bal Harbour's defining high-end Japanese restaurants. The polished room, luxury shopping setting and consistent sushi, robata and sake program make it a natural dinner for affluent locals and visitors staying north of Miami Beach.
highlights: Bal Harbour Shops Japanese dining with sushi, robata, polished service and a luxury retail setting.
sources: Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Carbone's Miami Beach outpost translates Major Food Group's red-sauce luxury into a high-demand South of Fifth room. The cooking is familiar and theatrical, but the service, wine spend and reservation heat make it one of the city's major affluent social dinners.
highlights: Glamorous Major Food Group Italian-American dining, tableside theatre and a high-demand South of Fifth crowd.
sources: Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

restaurant_name: The Den at Azabu Miami Beach
description: The Den is Azabu's intimate omakase counter tucked inside the Stanton South Beach complex. It gives Miami Beach another serious Japanese option, with a quieter and more traditional feel than the city's louder luxury sushi rooms.
highlights: Intimate South Beach omakase counter, Japanese technique and a luxury hotel-adjacent setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Financial Times; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Hiyakawa is a serene Wynwood Japanese restaurant that offers both sushi craft and a broader cooked menu. It works well for diners who want a polished Japanese evening without the full exclusivity or cost of Miami's tiniest omakase counters.
highlights: Michelin-selected Japanese restaurant in Wynwood with sushi, tasting-menu options and a serene design language.
sources: Michelin Guide; Financial Times; Eater Miami; Official website

description: Klaw is a high-end seafood and steak restaurant in Edgewater with bay views and a serious crustacean program. The room feels adult and expensive, making it a credible alternative for diners who want a grand seafood night rather than a tasting menu.
highlights: Upscale seafood and steak, king crab focus, bay views and a polished Edgewater dining room.
sources: Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Casa Tua is a South Beach classic for discreet glamour, Italian cooking and garden-room romance. Its private-club mood and long-running popularity with Miami's social set keep it relevant even as flashier rooms open around it.
highlights: South Beach garden dining, clubby Italian atmosphere and a long-standing affluent local following.
sources: Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Queen turns the historic Paris Theater into one of Miami Beach's most dramatic dinner rooms. The Japanese steakhouse menu, Champagne energy and cinematic architecture make it a design-conscious luxury choice when atmosphere matters as much as the food.
highlights: Japanese steakhouse in the restored Paris Theater with dramatic Art Deco architecture and a high-glamour crowd.
sources: Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Joe's is the Miami institution, open since 1913 and still central to the city's dining identity. The stone crabs, old-school service and South of Fifth ritual make it a relaxed night that affluent visitors and locals continue to treat as essential.
highlights: Historic South Beach seafood institution known for stone crabs, classic sides and a century-plus local role.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out; Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Official website

description: Mandolin remains one of Miami's most beloved relaxed dinner rooms, especially for affluent diners who want charm rather than formality. The courtyard, Greek-Turkish cooking and Design District bungalow setting give it a strong local identity.
highlights: Dreamy Design District courtyard, Greek and Turkish mezze, relaxed romance and enduring local popularity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out; Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Official website

description: Michael Schwartz's Design District restaurant helped define modern Miami dining long before the city's current luxury boom. It remains a dependable, ingredient-focused local classic with the ease and polish affluent regulars appreciate.
highlights: Design District pioneer with ingredient-driven cooking, neighborhood energy and a long-running local reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Macchialina is a serious Miami Beach trattoria with handmade pasta, Italian wines and a loyal local following. It is casual compared with the Michelin core, but the cooking and grown-up atmosphere make it a smart relaxed dinner for sophisticated diners.
highlights: Beloved Miami Beach trattoria with handmade pastas, Italian wine and a relaxed neighborhood feel.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website

description: Cafe La Trova captures Miami's Cuban identity with Michelle Bernstein-backed cooking, cocktails and live music in Little Havana. It is festive, but still a proper sit-down dinner that an affluent traveler can appreciate as a culturally specific local night out.
highlights: Little Havana Cuban restaurant with serious cocktails, live music, polished service and strong cultural identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater Miami; Miami New Times; Time Out; Official website
